---
title: "The impact of the Trade and Cooperation Agreement on UK trade"
description: "New econometric evidence that the UK-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement cut UK exports to the EU by over 22% and shrank export product variety."
date: "2023-06-14"
categories: [brexit]
---

With Jun Du, this piece sets out econometric evidence that the Trade and
Cooperation Agreement, in force since January 2021, is a major driver of the
UK's weak trade performance — not a neutral continuity arrangement. Exports
to the EU came in 22.1% lower and imports 9.5% lower than a no-Brexit
counterfactual would predict, and the UK lost an estimated 20–42% of its
export product variety over the first fifteen months, with small firms in
manufacturing regions hit hardest.

**Originally published on UK in a Changing Europe**, June 14, 2023.
